description: Currently valid SIGMETs – warnings of en-route weather hazardous to aircraft (thunderstorms, severe turbulence and icing, mountain waves, volcanic ash, tropical cyclones) – issued by meteorological watch offices worldwide and decoded into polygons by the Aviation Weather Center.

coverage.geographic: Worldwide flight information regions (international SIGMETs) plus United States domestic convective and non-convective SIGMETs.
coverage.temporal: SIGMETs valid at fetch time (typically valid for 2–6 hours); expired SIGMETs persist locally until retention expires.

updateCadence.upstream: Updated about once a minute as SIGMETs are received

attribution: NOAA/NWS Aviation Weather Center; SIGMETs issued by national meteorological watch offices

license.name: U.S. Government work – public domain (NWS disclaimer); underlying SIGMETs are ICAO operational messages issued by national meteorological watch offices
license.notes: The Data API page states no separate data licence and links to the NWS disclaimer (NWS web information is in the public domain unless noted otherwise). API usage rules: at most 100 requests per minute, keep requests limited in scope and frequency, set a custom User-Agent. This adapter makes one request every 5 minutes.

limitations: Not for flight planning or operational use: this is a situational-awareness view that can lag the official dissemination by several minutes.

Polygons are AWC's automatic decoding of free-text SIGMETs; a SIGMET whose area could not be decoded has no usable coordinates and is rejected, and decoded shapes are occasionally wrong or simplified.
A SIGMET describes a hazard within a flight-level band (attributes baseFt/topFt), not weather at the surface.

The documentation marks the older /api/data/isigmet (international only) endpoint as deprecated; this adapter uses its documented successor /api/data/sigmet, which also returns U.S. domestic SIGMETs (hazard CONV = convective SIGMET).
The API returns at most 400 entries per request.
confidenceNotes: Severity is derived by this application from the hazard and its qualifier and expresses the danger to aircraft, not surface impact: tropical cyclone 4; volcanic ash 3; severe (SEV) turbulence, icing or mountain wave 3; frequent (FRQ) or squall-line (SQL) thunderstorms and heavy (HVY) dust or sand storms 3; other thunderstorm, convective, dust and sand SIGMETs 2. Confidence is derived from whether the phenomenon is reported as observed (OBS, 0.9) or forecast (FCST, 0.7); SIGMETs without that flag carry no confidence.

retention.note: SIGMETs are kept for 3 days after their validity ends, then purged.

layers.name: Aviation SIGMETs
layers.description: Areas with weather hazardous to aircraft (thunderstorms, severe turbulence / icing, volcanic ash, tropical cyclones) according to currently valid SIGMETs.
